stem: A random sample of 200 adults in a city is selected, and 84 of them say that they ride the bus at least once a week. Which of the following is the point estimate of the proportion of all adults in the city who ride the bus at least once a week?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Nothing in the sample points to 0.50. The point estimate is the sample proportion.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The sample proportion is a point estimator of the population proportion: 84 / 200 = 0.42.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the sample proportion of the adults who do not ride the bus at least once a week.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This is the number of adults in the sample who ride the bus, not a proportion.

explanation: The point estimate is p̂ = 84 / 200 = 0.42.

stem: Which of the following is the best description of an unbiased estimator of a population parameter?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An estimator that is calculated from a sample that is larger than 10% of the population from which the sample was selected
choices.explanation: The size of the sample compared with the population is not what makes an estimator unbiased.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An estimator that gives exactly the value of the population parameter whenever it is calculated from any random sample of the population
choices.explanation: An unbiased estimator varies from sample to sample. Only its average is right.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An estimator whose values are always less than the value of the population parameter that it is used to estimate from the sample
choices.explanation: That describes an estimator that underestimates, which is biased.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An estimator whose values, on average over repeated random samples, neither underestimate nor overestimate the parameter
choices.explanation: An estimator is unbiased if on average the value of the estimator does not underestimate or overestimate the parameter.

explanation: An unbiased estimator is correct on average over many random samples.

stem: A statistician takes many random samples of size 50 from a population in which the proportion is 0.30. The mean of all of the sample proportions is 0.301. Which of the following is the best conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The sample proportion is a biased estimator that overestimates the population proportion, because the mean of 0.301 is greater than 0.30
choices.explanation: The difference of 0.001 is small enough to be explained by chance in a simulation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The sample proportion is an unbiased estimator, because every sample proportion in the simulation of random samples is exactly equal to 0.30
choices.explanation: The sample proportions vary from sample to sample. It is their mean that is close to 0.30.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The sample proportion is a biased estimator, because the mean of the sample proportions in the simulation is not exactly equal to 0.30
choices.explanation: A simulation gives a mean that is close to, but not exactly, the center, because of chance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The sample proportion appears to be an unbiased estimator of the population proportion, because its mean is very close to 0.30
choices.explanation: The center of the distribution of the sample proportions is the population proportion, so the estimator does not under- or overestimate on average.

explanation: The mean of the sampling distribution is about the parameter, so p-hat is unbiased.

stem: The values of a statistic from many random samples have a distribution that is centered at 0.35, but the value of the population parameter that it is used to estimate is 0.30. Which of the following is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The statistic is a biased estimator that, on average, underestimates the parameter
choices.explanation: The center, 0.35, is greater than the parameter, 0.30, so it overestimates.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The statistic is an unbiased estimator, because the values of the statistic from different samples are different
choices.explanation: Variation from sample to sample does not make an estimator biased. The center matters.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The statistic is an unbiased estimator, because its center is close to the parameter
choices.explanation: A difference of 0.05 in the center means that the estimator is biased.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The statistic is a biased estimator that, on average, overestimates the parameter
choices.explanation: The center of its distribution is greater than the parameter, so it overestimates on average.

explanation: A statistic with a center above the parameter overestimates on average: it is biased.

stem: Which symbol is used for the point estimator of the population proportion p?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The sample standard deviation, s
choices.explanation: The sample standard deviation estimates a population standard deviation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The sample proportion, p̂
choices.explanation: The sample proportion p-hat is the point estimator for the population proportion p.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The sample mean, x̄
choices.explanation: The sample mean is the point estimator for a population mean.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The population proportion, p
choices.explanation: The parameter p is what is estimated, not the estimator.

explanation: p-hat is the point estimator of p.

stem: A researcher says, "My estimator is unbiased, so the value that I calculated from my random sample must be equal to the population parameter." Which of the following is the best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The statement is incorrect, because an estimator that is unbiased cannot be calculated from a random sample
choices.explanation: Unbiased estimators are calculated from random samples.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The statement is incorrect: an unbiased estimator is right on average, but the value from a single sample usually differs from the parameter
choices.explanation: Unbiased describes the center of the sampling distribution, not each value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The statement is correct, because the sample was random, so the value of the estimator is guaranteed to be right and equal to the value of the parameter
choices.explanation: Random selection removes bias but does not make a single estimate exact.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The statement is correct, because an unbiased estimator never differs from the parameter for a random sample
choices.explanation: Values of an unbiased estimator vary from sample to sample.

explanation: Unbiased: correct on average. One sample's estimate has sampling variability.

stem: In a large population, the proportion of adults who have a pet is p = 0.30. Random samples of size 100 are selected. What are the mean and the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample proportion p̂?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The mean is 0.30 and the standard deviation is 0.0458

choices.label: B
choices.text: The mean is 30 and the standard deviation is 4.5826
choices.explanation: These are the mean and standard deviation of the count of adults with a pet, np and the square root of np(1 - p), not of the proportion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The mean is 0.30 and the standard deviation is 0.0021
choices.explanation: The value 0.0021 is the variance, p(1 - p) / n. The standard deviation is its square root.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The mean is 0.30 and the standard deviation is 0.4583
choices.explanation: This is √(p(1 - p)), which leaves out the division by the sample size.

stem: A school has 1,500 students. A researcher plans to select a random sample of 200 students without replacement, to estimate the proportion of the students who walk to school. Which of the following is correct about the 10% condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The condition is not met, because the sample size of 200 is more than 10% of the population size of 1,500
choices.explanation: The 10% condition requires n ≤ N / 10 = 150.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The condition is not met, because a sample of students must be selected with replacement
choices.explanation: The 10% condition is for samples taken without replacement. Replacement is not required.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The condition is met, because the sample was selected at random from the students at the school, and a random sample always meets it
choices.explanation: Random selection is the randomization condition. The 10% condition is about the size of the sample.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The condition is met, because the sample size of 200 is greater than 30
choices.explanation: A sample size above 30 does not satisfy the 10% condition.

explanation: n = 200 is greater than 10% of 1,500, which is 150.

stem: Random samples of size 40 are selected from a very large population in which the proportion of successes is p = 0.10. Is the sampling distribution of the sample proportion p̂ approximately normal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No, because np = 40(0.10) = 4 is less than 10
choices.explanation: The expected number of successes should be at least 10 (and the expected number of failures should be at least 10).

choices.label: B
choices.text: No, because the population is very large, which is not allowed in the conditions
choices.explanation: A large population is not a problem. The problem is the expected number of successes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes, because the sample size 40 is greater than 30
choices.explanation: For a sample proportion, the condition uses np and n(1 - p), not just the sample size.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yes, because n(1 - p) = 40(0.90) = 36 is greater than 10
choices.explanation: Both np and n(1 - p) must be at least 10, and np = 4.

explanation: np = 4 < 10, so the normal approximation is not appropriate.

stem: In a large population, the proportion of voters who support a measure is 0.60. A random sample of 150 voters is selected. What is the approximate probability that the sample proportion who support the measure is greater than 0.65?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the probability that the sample proportion is less than 0.65, the complement.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The sampling distribution is approximately normal with mean 0.60 and standard deviation 0.0400. z = (0.65 - 0.60) / 0.0400 = 1.25.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This divides by √(p(1 - p)) and leaves out the sample size, which gives a standard deviation that is too large.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This is the probability that the sample proportion is greater than the mean, 0.60.

stem: The standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample proportion of adults with a pet, for random samples of size 100, is 0.0458. Which of the following is the correct interpretation of this value?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In random samples of 100 adults, the sample proportion typically varies from the population proportion by about 0.0458
choices.explanation: The standard deviation of a sampling distribution quantifies the typical amount that the statistic varies from the parameter.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In every random sample of 100 adults, the sample proportion is within 0.0458 of the population proportion of adults who have a pet
choices.explanation: Some sample proportions are farther away. The standard deviation is a typical distance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The population proportion of adults with a pet is 0.0458
choices.explanation: The standard deviation of the sampling distribution is not the population proportion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 4.58% of the adults in each random sample of 100 have a pet
choices.explanation: That would be a sample proportion. The standard deviation describes how the sample proportions vary.

explanation: The standard deviation of p-hat is the typical distance of p-hat from p in repeated samples.

stem: Random samples are selected from a large population with proportion p. The sample size is increased from 100 to 400. What happens to the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample proportion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It does not change, because the population proportion p stays the same when the sample size changes
choices.explanation: The sample size is in the formula, so the standard deviation changes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is divided by 2, because the standard deviation includes √n and √400 is 2 times √100
choices.explanation: The sample size is multiplied by 4, so the standard deviation is multiplied by 1/2.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is divided by 4, because the sample size is multiplied by 4
choices.explanation: The standard deviation involves the square root of n, so it is divided by 2 and not by 4.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is multiplied by 2, because a larger sample varies more from sample to sample
choices.explanation: A larger sample varies less from sample to sample.

explanation: σ is proportional to 1 / √n: quadrupling n halves σ.

stem: A researcher wants to use the sampling distribution of a sample proportion. The researcher selects the first 60 people who walk into a store. Which condition for the sampling distribution is most clearly violated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The 10% condition, because 60 people is more than 10% of the population of all of the customers who might walk in
choices.explanation: Nothing says the sample is more than 10% of the population. The problem is how it was selected.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The condition that p must be 0.5, because the people who walk in are of two types
choices.explanation: There is no condition that p = 0.5.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The condition that the sample size must be greater than 30, because 60 is too small a sample
choices.explanation: 60 is not less than 30. The issue is the method of selection.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The randomization condition, because the people who walk in first were not selected by a random method
choices.explanation: The data should be collected using a random sample.

explanation: A convenience sample is not random: the randomization condition is violated.

stem: The sampling distribution of the sample proportion p̂ for random samples of size 80 has mean 0.40. What is the probability that p̂ is less than 0.40, assuming that the distribution is approximately normal?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the mean of the distribution, not a probability.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The distribution is approximately normal and symmetric about its mean, 0.40, so half of the values are less than 0.40.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A probability of 0.05 would be for a value 1.645 standard deviations below the mean, not for the mean itself.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This is the probability that p-hat is within 1 standard deviation of the mean.

explanation: By symmetry about the mean, P(p-hat < 0.40) = 0.50.

stem: In a large population, p = 0.30. A random sample of 200 is selected. Which of the following is the approximate probability that the sample proportion is between 0.26 and 0.34?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the area within 2 standard deviations. The boundaries here are about 1.23 standard deviations from the mean.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the area to the left of z = 1.23. It includes the area below 0.26.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: σ = √(0.30(0.70) / 200) = 0.0324, so the boundaries are z = ±1.23, and the area between them is about 0.78.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This is the area within 1 standard deviation. The boundaries here are about 1.23 standard deviations from the mean.

stem: A researcher selects a random sample of 400 students from a large school and finds the proportion of the students in the sample who own a bicycle. The researcher wants to estimate the proportion of all students at the school who own a bicycle. Which procedure is appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A one-sample z-test for a population proportion
choices.explanation: A test answers a question about whether the proportion differs from a specified value. The goal here is to estimate it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A chi-square test for independence
choices.explanation: A chi-square test is for categorical variables in a two-way table, not for an interval estimate of one proportion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A one-sample z-interval for a population proportion
choices.explanation: The parameter is a single population proportion, estimated from one random sample.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A two-sample z-interval for a difference between population proportions
choices.explanation: There is only one sample and one population, so there is no difference between two proportions.

explanation: The goal is to estimate one population proportion: a one-sample z-interval.

stem: A random sample of 400 students from a large school is selected, and the proportion who own a bicycle is used to construct a confidence interval. Which of the following correctly states the parameter?

choices.label: A
choices.text: p̂ = the proportion of the 400 students in the sample who own a bicycle
choices.explanation: This is the sample proportion, a statistic, and not the parameter.

choices.label: B
choices.text: p = the proportion of all students at the school who own a bicycle
choices.explanation: The parameter references the proportion, the response variable and the population in context.

choices.label: C
choices.text: p = the number of students in the sample at the school who own a bicycle
choices.explanation: A proportion is not a count.

choices.label: D
choices.text: p = the proportion of the 400 students in the sample who do not own a bicycle
choices.explanation: The parameter is about the population, and about owning a bicycle.

explanation: The parameter is the proportion of all students at the school who own a bicycle.

stem: Which of the following lists the conditions that must be verified for a one-sample z-interval for a population proportion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The sample is random; the sample size is at least 10% of the population; and the number of successes and failures in the sample are each at least 5
choices.explanation: The sample size should be at most 10% of the population, and the counts should be at least 10.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The two samples are independent; the sample sizes are at most 10% of the populations; and the expected counts are each greater than 5
choices.explanation: Those are for other procedures. A one-sample interval has a single sample.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The sample is random; the sample size is at most 10% of the population; and the observed numbers of successes and failures are each at least 10
choices.explanation: These are the randomization, 10% and normality conditions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The sample is random; the population is approximately normal in shape; and the sample size is greater than 30, so the counts do not matter
choices.explanation: For a proportion, the condition is on the counts of successes and failures, not on a normal population.

explanation: Randomization, 10% condition, and at least 10 observed successes and failures.

stem: In a random sample of 400 students from a large school, 180 own a bicycle. Which of the following is a 95% confidence interval for the proportion of all students at the school who own a bicycle?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This uses the variance of the sample proportion instead of the standard error.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This uses $z^*$ = 1.645, which is for a 90% confidence level.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This leaves out the division by the sample size in the standard error.

stem: Which of the following is the critical value $z^*$ for a 99% confidence interval for a population proportion?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the critical value for a 95% confidence level.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The middle 99% of the standard normal distribution lies between -2.576 and 2.576.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the z-score with 1% of the area above it, which is for a 98% confidence level.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This is the critical value for a 90% confidence level.

explanation: $z^*$ = 2.576 for 99% confidence.

stem: In a random sample of 400 students, the sample proportion who own a bicycle is 0.45. What is the standard error of the sample proportion?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This leaves out the division by the sample size.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the margin of error for a 95% confidence level, not the standard error.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is p-hat(1 - p-hat) / n, the variance, before taking the square root.

stem: A researcher wants to estimate a population proportion with a 95% confidence level and a margin of error of no more than 0.03. There is no prior estimate of the proportion. What is the minimum sample size needed?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Use p-hat = 0.5 for the upper bound: n = (1.96 / 0.03)²(0.5)(0.5) = 1067.1, so the sample size is 1,068.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This divides by the margin of error instead of by its square.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is one-fourth of the correct sample size, which comes from leaving out the factor of 4 in 1 / 0.5².

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The sample size must be rounded up to the next whole number, so that the margin of error is no more than 0.03.

explanation: n ≥ ($z^*$ / MOE)² p-hat(1 - p-hat) = 1067.1, so use 1,068.

stem: In a random sample of 80 adults from a large city, 6 say that they own a motorcycle. A student wants to construct a one-sample z-interval for the proportion of all adults in the city who own a motorcycle. Which of the following is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The normality condition is not met, because the observed number of successes, 6, is less than 10
choices.explanation: The number of observed successes and the number of observed failures must each be at least 10.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The randomization condition is not met, because only 6 of the 80 adults in the sample own a motorcycle
choices.explanation: The number of adults who own a motorcycle does not decide whether the sample was selected at random.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The 10% condition is not met, because 80 is greater than 6
choices.explanation: The 10% condition compares the sample size with the population size.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All conditions are met, because the sample is random and the sample size is greater than 30
choices.explanation: The normality condition uses the counts of successes and failures, and 6 is less than 10.

explanation: n p-hat = 6 < 10, so the normality condition fails.

stem: Which of the following is a correct statement of the margin of error for a one-sample z-interval for a population proportion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is the width of the interval, and equals the critical value $z^*$ divided by the standard error of the sample proportion
choices.explanation: The margin of error is half the width, and it is a product with the standard error.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is half the width of the interval, and equals the critical value $z^*$ times the standard error of the sample proportion
choices.explanation: The margin of error is $z^*$√(p-hat(1 - p-hat) / n).

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is the standard error of the sample proportion, and equals the sample proportion divided by the square root of n
choices.explanation: The standard error is not the margin of error. The margin of error is $z^*$ times the standard error.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is half the width of the interval, and equals the sample proportion times the critical value $z^*$
choices.explanation: The margin of error multiplies $z^*$ by the standard error, not by the sample proportion.

explanation: MOE = $z^*$ × SE, half the width of the interval.

stem: A 95% confidence interval for the proportion of all students at a school who own a bicycle is (0.401, 0.499). Which of the following is a correct interpretation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 95% of all of the sample proportions from random samples of 400 students are between 0.401 and 0.499
choices.explanation: The interval is not a range for the sample proportions of other samples.

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 95% of the students at the school own a bicycle, because the interval is between 0.401 and 0.499
choices.explanation: The interval estimates a proportion. It does not say that 95% of the students own a bicycle.

choices.label: C
choices.text: We are 95% confident that the interval from 0.401 to 0.499 contains the proportion of all students at the school who own a bicycle
choices.explanation: An interpretation references the parameter, the population and the context.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is a 95% probability that the proportion of the students in the sample who own a bicycle is between 0.401 and 0.499
choices.explanation: The sample proportion, 0.45, is known. The interval is about the population proportion.

explanation: Interpret the interval as a statement of confidence about the population proportion.

stem: Which of the following is the correct interpretation of a 95% confidence level for a population proportion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In repeated random sampling with the same sample size, about 95% of the intervals calculated will capture the population proportion
choices.explanation: The confidence level describes the long-run success rate of the method.

choices.label: B
choices.text: There is a 95% probability that the population proportion is in the one interval that was calculated from the sample that was selected
choices.explanation: The population proportion is a fixed value. The interval from one sample either contains it or does not.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In repeated random sampling, approximately 95% of the sample proportions are equal to the population proportion
choices.explanation: Most sample proportions differ from the population proportion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In any one random sample, 95% of the values are within the interval that was calculated from the sample
choices.explanation: The interval is for the population proportion, not for the individual values.

explanation: A 95% confidence level means that about 95% of the intervals from repeated random samples capture the parameter.

stem: A random sample of 500 adults is used to construct a 95% confidence interval for the proportion of all adults in a city who support a tax. The interval is (0.36, 0.44). A mayor claims that the proportion of all adults in the city who support the tax is 0.50. Which of the following is the best conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The interval provides convincing evidence that the proportion is 0.50, because 0.50 is close to the interval
choices.explanation: A value outside the interval is not plausible, however close it is.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The interval provides convincing evidence that the proportion is 0.40, because 0.40 is the center of the interval that was calculated
choices.explanation: The interval gives a range of plausible values. It does not prove a single value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The interval provides convincing evidence that the proportion is not 0.50, because 0.50 is not in the interval of plausible values
choices.explanation: Values outside the interval are not plausible values for the proportion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The interval does not provide any evidence about the claim, because a confidence interval cannot be used to evaluate a claim
choices.explanation: An interval gives plausible values and can support a claim.

explanation: 0.50 is not in (0.36, 0.44), so it is not a plausible value for the proportion.

stem: A 95% confidence interval for the proportion of all registered voters in a state who support a measure is (0.46, 0.54). Which of the following claims is supported by the interval?

choices.label: A
choices.text: There is convincing evidence that fewer than half of the voters support the measure, because the interval has values below 0.50
choices.explanation: The interval also has values above 0.50, so neither claim is supported.

choices.label: B
choices.text: There is convincing evidence that a majority of the voters support the measure, because the center of the interval is 0.50
choices.explanation: The center is 0.50, but the interval includes values less than 0.50.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There is not convincing evidence that a majority of the voters support the measure, because 0.50 is in the interval
choices.explanation: Plausible values include proportions below 0.50, so the interval does not support a claim of a majority.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is convincing evidence that exactly 50% of the voters support the measure, because 0.50 is in the interval of plausible values
choices.explanation: An interval gives a range of plausible values, not a proof of one value.

explanation: 0.50 is a plausible value, so the interval does not show a majority.

stem: A student constructs a 90% confidence interval and a 99% confidence interval for a population proportion, using the same random sample. Which of the following is true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The 90% interval is wider, because it is less likely to contain the parameter
choices.explanation: A lower confidence level gives a narrower interval.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The 99% interval is wider, because a greater confidence level has a greater critical value and a greater margin of error

choices.label: C
choices.text: The 99% interval is narrower, because it is more likely to contain the parameter
choices.explanation: To be more confident, the interval must be wider.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The two intervals have the same width, because they are calculated from the same sample and the same sample size
choices.explanation: The critical values differ, so the margins of error differ.

explanation: For the same sample, a higher confidence level gives a larger critical value and a wider interval.

stem: A 95% confidence interval for a population proportion, based on a random sample of 100, has a width of about 0.196. About what would the width be for a random sample of 400, with the same sample proportion and the same confidence level?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 0.098, because the width is approximately proportional to 1 / √n, and √400 is 2 times √100
choices.explanation: Quadrupling the sample size halves the width.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 0.196, because the confidence level and the sample proportion did not change when the sample size changed
choices.explanation: The sample size is in the standard error, so the width changes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 0.049, because the width is divided by 4 when the sample size is multiplied by 4
choices.explanation: The width is proportional to 1 / √n, so it is divided by 2, not by 4.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 0.392, because a larger sample gives a larger margin of error
choices.explanation: A larger sample gives a smaller margin of error.

explanation: Width is about proportional to 1 / √n: 0.196 / 2 = 0.098.

stem: Two intervals are calculated from the same random sample: one for a 95% confidence level and one for a 90% confidence level. The sample proportion is 0.40 and the sample size is 300. A student says that the 90% interval gives a more precise estimate and is therefore better. Which of the following is the best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The 90% interval is narrower and captures the parameter more often, so it is better in every way for estimating the proportion
choices.explanation: A lower confidence level captures the parameter less often.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The two intervals are equally good, because they are calculated from the same random sample
choices.explanation: The two have different widths and different confidence levels.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The 90% interval is wider but more precise, because it uses a smaller critical value
choices.explanation: A smaller critical value gives a narrower interval, not a wider one.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The 90% interval is narrower, but the method that produced it captures the parameter less often (about 90% of the time)
choices.explanation: There is a trade-off between the width of the interval and the confidence level.

explanation: A narrower interval comes with a lower confidence level.

stem: A 95% confidence interval for the proportion of all households in a city that recycle is (0.58, 0.66). A city official claims that more than half of the households recycle. Does the interval provide convincing evidence for the claim?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, because the sample proportion, 0.62, is more than 0.50 in the sample of households
choices.explanation: The sample proportion is above 0.50, but it is the interval that shows convincing evidence about the population.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, because all of the plausible values in the interval are greater than 0.50
choices.explanation: The interval (0.58, 0.66) does not contain 0.50 or any value less than 0.50.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No, because the interval contains values that are less than its upper limit of 0.66
choices.explanation: Values within the interval being less than its upper limit is always true and does not argue against the claim.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No, because a confidence interval can only be used for a claim about a difference between two proportions
choices.explanation: An interval for a single proportion can support a claim about that proportion.

explanation: Every plausible value is above 0.50, so the interval supports the claim.

stem: A company claims that 90% of its customers are satisfied. A consumer group selects a random sample of 300 customers and wants to test whether the proportion of all of the company's customers who are satisfied is different from 0.90. Which procedure is appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A two-sample z-test for the difference between two population proportions
choices.explanation: There is one sample and one population, not two.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A one-sample z-test for a population proportion
choices.explanation: The parameter is one population proportion and it is compared with a specified value, 0.90.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A one-sample z-interval for a population proportion
choices.explanation: An interval estimates a proportion. This question asks about a specific claimed value, so a test is used.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A chi-square test for homogeneity
choices.explanation: A chi-square test compares distributions of a categorical variable across populations in a two-way table.

explanation: A test about one proportion compared with a stated value: a one-sample z-test.

stem: A manufacturer claims that at most 5% of its light bulbs are defective. An inspector believes that the proportion of all of the bulbs that are defective is greater than 5%, and plans to test the claim. Which of the following are the correct hypotheses?

choices.label: A
choices.text: H₀: p = 0.05 and Hₐ: p < 0.05, where p is the proportion of all of the manufacturer's bulbs that are defective
choices.explanation: The inspector believes that the proportion is greater than 0.05, not less than 0.05.

choices.label: B
choices.text: H₀: p > 0.05 and Hₐ: p = 0.05, where p is the proportion of all of the manufacturer's bulbs that are defective
choices.explanation: The null hypothesis contains the equality, and the alternative is the belief.

choices.label: C
choices.text: H₀: p̂ = 0.05 and Hₐ: p̂ > 0.05, where p̂ is the proportion of the bulbs in the sample that are defective
choices.explanation: Hypotheses are about a population parameter, p, not about a sample statistic.

choices.label: D
choices.text: H₀: p = 0.05 and Hₐ: p > 0.05, where p is the proportion of all of the manufacturer's bulbs that are defective
choices.explanation: The null hypothesis is the status quo with an equality, and the alternative is the inspector's belief.

stem: A school board wants to know whether the proportion of all students at a large school who take the bus has changed from last year's value of 0.40. Which of the following are the correct hypotheses?

choices.label: A
choices.text: H₀: p = 0.40 and Hₐ: p < 0.40, where p is the proportion of all students at the school who take the bus now
choices.explanation: Nothing says that the proportion decreased. The question is whether it changed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: H₀: p = 0.40 and Hₐ: p ≠ 0.40, where p is the proportion of all students at the school who take the bus now
choices.explanation: The question asks whether the proportion has changed, in either direction, so the alternative is two-sided.

choices.label: C
choices.text: H₀: p = 0.40 and Hₐ: p > 0.40, where p is the proportion of all students at the school who take the bus now
choices.explanation: Nothing says that the proportion increased. The question is whether it changed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: H₀: p ≠ 0.40 and Hₐ: p = 0.40, where p is the proportion of all students at the school who take the bus now
choices.explanation: The null hypothesis has the equality, and the alternative says that there is a change.

explanation: A change in either direction is a two-sided alternative: p ≠ 0.40.

stem: A researcher will test a claim about the proportion of all adults in a city who exercise regularly. Which of the following is the best way to define the parameter in context?

choices.label: A
choices.text: p = the proportion of adults who exercise
choices.explanation: This does not state the population, the adults in the city.

choices.label: B
choices.text: p = the number of adults in the city who exercise regularly
choices.explanation: A parameter for this test is a proportion, not a count.

choices.label: C
choices.text: p = the proportion of all adults in the city who exercise regularly
choices.explanation: The parameter references the proportion, the response variable and the population.

choices.label: D
choices.text: p = the proportion of the adults in the sample who exercise regularly
choices.explanation: That is the sample proportion, a statistic.

explanation: The parameter is the proportion of all adults in the city who exercise regularly.

stem: For a one-sample z-test for a population proportion with the null hypothesis H₀: p = p₀, how is the normality condition checked?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The observed numbers of successes and failures in the sample should each be at least 10, whatever p₀ is
choices.explanation: That is the condition for a confidence interval. For a test, use the null value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The sample size should be greater than 30, whatever the value of p₀
choices.explanation: The condition uses the expected counts, not only the sample size.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The expected numbers of successes and failures should each be greater than 5
choices.explanation: Greater than 5 is the expected counts condition for a chi-square test, not for a z-test for a proportion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The expected numbers of successes and failures, n p₀ and n(1 - p₀), should each be at least 10
choices.explanation: The test is done assuming the null hypothesis is true, so the null value p₀ is used.

explanation: For the z-test, check n p0 ≥ 10 and n(1 - p0) ≥ 10.

stem: A random sample of 150 bulbs is selected from a very large shipment, to test H₀: p = 0.05 where p is the proportion of all bulbs in the shipment that are defective. Is the normality condition for the one-sample z-test met?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, because the sample size of 150 is greater than 30
choices.explanation: The condition is about the expected counts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No, because the expected number of defective bulbs, 150(0.05) = 7.5, is less than 10
choices.explanation: The expected number of successes under H0 must be at least 10.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes, because the expected number of non-defective bulbs, 150(0.95) = 142.5, is greater than 10
choices.explanation: Both expected counts must be at least 10, and the expected number of defective bulbs is 7.5.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No, because the sample size, 150, is more than 10% of a very large shipment
choices.explanation: A sample of 150 from a very large shipment is less than 10% of it.

explanation: n p0 = 7.5 < 10: the normality condition is not met.

stem: A student writes the hypotheses H₀: p̂ = 0.60 and Hₐ: p̂ < 0.60 for a test about the proportion of all voters who support a measure, where p̂ is the proportion who support it in a sample of 400 voters. What is the error?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The alternative hypothesis must always be two-sided, with p̂ ≠ 0.60
choices.explanation: An alternative hypothesis can be one-sided.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The null hypothesis should have the inequality p̂ > 0.60, and the alternative should have the equality
choices.explanation: The null hypothesis has the equality.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There is no error, because a sample statistic is used to carry out the test of the claim
choices.explanation: The statistic is used in the test statistic, but the hypotheses are about the parameter.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The hypotheses are about the sample proportion, but they should be about the population proportion p
choices.explanation: Hypotheses are statements about a population parameter.

explanation: Hypotheses use the parameter p, not the statistic p-hat.

stem: Which of the following is the best description of the null hypothesis in a hypothesis test for a population proportion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The statement that the researcher can prove to be true by using the sample data
choices.explanation: A test can never prove that the null hypothesis is true.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The statement about the parameter that is assumed to be correct unless there is convincing statistical evidence otherwise
choices.explanation: It is the status quo, and it contains an equality.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The claim or belief about the parameter for which the researcher is collecting evidence in the study and hopes to support with the data
choices.explanation: That describes the alternative hypothesis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The statement that the sample proportion is equal to the population proportion
choices.explanation: Both hypotheses are about the population parameter, not the sample statistic.

explanation: H0 is the status quo that is assumed unless the evidence is convincing.

stem: In a test of H₀: p = 0.50 versus Hₐ: p > 0.50, where p is the proportion of all voters in a state who support a measure, the p-value is 0.008. Which of the following is the correct interpretation of the p-value?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Assuming that the proportion of all voters in the state who support the measure is 0.50, the probability of getting a sample proportion as large as the one observed, or larger, is 0.008
choices.explanation: The p-value is computed assuming that the null hypothesis is true.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The probability that the proportion of all voters who support the measure is greater than 0.50 is 0.992
choices.explanation: The p-value does not give the probability of the alternative hypothesis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The probability that the proportion of all voters in the state who support the measure is 0.50 is 0.008
choices.explanation: The p-value is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assuming that the proportion of all voters in the state who support the measure is greater than 0.50, the probability of getting the sample proportion that was observed in the random sample is 0.008
choices.explanation: The p-value is computed assuming the null value, not assuming the alternative.

explanation: A p-value is a probability about the data, computed assuming H0 is true.

stem: A test of a population proportion gives a small p-value. Which of the following is the best interpretation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The sample was selected incorrectly, because a sample should not give a small p-value
choices.explanation: A small p-value is not a sign of an incorrect sample.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The observed value of the test statistic would be likely if the null hypothesis were true
choices.explanation: A small p-value means that the result would be unlikely if H0 were true.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The null hypothesis is certain to be false, and the alternative hypothesis is certain to be true in this test
choices.explanation: A p-value gives evidence, not certainty.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The observed value of the test statistic would be unusual if the null hypothesis were true, which is evidence for the alternative
choices.explanation: The smaller the p-value, the more convincing the evidence for the alternative.

explanation: A small p-value: the result would be unusual under H0, which supports Ha.

stem: A test of H₀: p = 0.40 versus Hₐ: p > 0.40 gives a p-value of 0.31. Which of the following is the best conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The p-value is large, so there is convincing evidence for the alternative hypothesis about the population
choices.explanation: A large p-value does not support the alternative.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The p-value is not small, so there is not convincing evidence for the alternative hypothesis, and this is not evidence that the null hypothesis is true
choices.explanation: A large p-value fails to support Ha, but it does not show that H0 is true.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The p-value is 0.31, so the probability that the null hypothesis is true is 0.31
choices.explanation: The p-value is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The p-value is large, so there is convincing evidence that the null hypothesis is true for the population in the study
choices.explanation: A large p-value is not evidence for the null hypothesis.

explanation: A large p-value: no convincing evidence for Ha, and no evidence that H0 is true.

stem: The test statistic for a one-sample z-test is z = 2.10. What is the p-value if the alternative hypothesis is Hₐ: p ≠ p₀ (a two-sided test)?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the one-sided p-value, for the alternative Hₐ: p > p₀ only.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This halves the one-sided p-value instead of doubling it.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the probability of a z-score less than 2.10. A p-value is a tail probability.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The two-sided p-value is P(z ≤ -2.10) + P(z ≥ 2.10) = 2(0.0179).

stem: The test statistic for a one-sample z-test is z = -1.65. What is the p-value if the alternative hypothesis is Hₐ: p < p₀?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is 1 minus the two-sided p-value, which is not a tail probability.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the two-sided p-value. The alternative here is one-sided.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is P(z ≥ -1.65), the upper tail, which is the wrong direction for this alternative.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: For a lower-tail alternative, the p-value is P(z ≤ -1.65).

stem: A test has H₀: p = 0.50 and Hₐ: p > 0.50. The observed sample proportion, from a random sample of size 100, is 0.60. The dotplot shows 100 sample proportions from simulated random samples of size 100 when p = 0.50. Based on the simulation, what is the estimated p-value?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the proportion of the simulated sample proportions that are less than 0.60: 96 / 100.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This counts only the simulated proportions that are exactly 0.60: 1 / 100.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: 4 of the 100 simulated sample proportions are 0.60 or greater, as extreme or more extreme in the direction of the alternative.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This doubles the proportion, which is for a two-sided alternative. The alternative here is p > 0.50.

explanation: Estimated p-value = 4 / 100 = 0.040.

diagram.altText: Dotplot of the sample proportions from 100 simulated random samples of size 100 from a population in which p = 0.50.

stem: Two different tests of two different claims about population proportions have p-values of 0.003 and 0.04. Which of the following is the best comparison of the evidence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The test with the p-value of 0.003 shows that its null hypothesis is certainly false, and the other test shows that its null hypothesis is true
choices.explanation: A p-value gives strength of evidence, not certainty.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The two tests provide the same evidence, because both p-values are less than 0.05
choices.explanation: Both are small, but the smaller one is more convincing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The test with the p-value of 0.04 provides more convincing evidence, because 0.04 is closer to the significance level of 0.05
choices.explanation: A p-value closer to 0.05 is weaker evidence.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The test with the p-value of 0.003 provides more convincing evidence for its alternative than the test with the p-value of 0.04
choices.explanation: The lower the p-value, the more convincing the evidence for the alternative.

explanation: A smaller p-value is more convincing evidence for the alternative.

stem: A random sample of 100 voters is selected, and 62 of them support a measure. A test has H₀: p = 0.50 and Hₐ: p > 0.50, where p is the proportion of all voters who support the measure. What is the value of the test statistic?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: The difference is taken in the wrong order. A sample proportion above p₀ gives a positive z.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This uses the sample proportion in the standard error. For a test, use the null value p₀.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This leaves out the division by the sample size in the standard error.

stem: A one-sample z-test of H₀: p = 0.50 versus Hₐ: p > 0.50 gives z = 2.40. Which of the following is the p-value?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This is the two-sided p-value. The alternative is one-sided.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the area to the left of z = 2.40, not the tail probability.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the height of the normal curve at z = 2.40, not an area.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The p-value is the area to the right of z = 2.40 under the standard normal curve.

stem: A test has a p-value of 0.0082. The significance level is α = 0.05. Which of the following is the correct decision and its meaning?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reject the null hypothesis, because the p-value is greater than α; the result is not statistically significant
choices.explanation: The p-value is less than α, not greater.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fail to reject the null hypothesis, because the p-value is less than 1
choices.explanation: The decision compares the p-value with α, not with 1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fail to reject the null hypothesis, because the p-value is very small
choices.explanation: A small p-value less than α leads to rejecting the null hypothesis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reject the null hypothesis, because the p-value is less than α; the result is statistically significant
choices.explanation: A p-value less than α means reject H0.

explanation: p-value 0.0082 < α = 0.05: reject H0.

stem: A test of H₀: p = 0.50 versus Hₐ: p > 0.50, where p is the proportion of all voters in a state who support a measure, has a p-value of 0.0082. Which of the following is the best conclusion at the 0.05 significance level?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It has been proved that more than 50% of all voters in the state support the measure
choices.explanation: A test does not prove a claim. The language should be non-definitive.

choices.label: B
choices.text: There is convincing statistical evidence that the proportion of all voters in the state who support the measure is greater than 0.50
choices.explanation: The conclusion is in context, in terms of the alternative hypothesis, and uses non-definitive language.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There is convincing statistical evidence that the proportion of the voters in the sample who support the measure is greater than 0.50
choices.explanation: The conclusion is about the population proportion, not about the sample.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is not convincing statistical evidence that the proportion of all voters in the state who support the measure is greater than 0.50
choices.explanation: With a p-value below α, there is convincing evidence for the alternative.

explanation: Reject H0: convincing evidence that p > 0.50, in context.

stem: A test of H₀: p = 0.30 versus Hₐ: p ≠ 0.30, where p is the proportion of all students at a school who walk to school, has a p-value of 0.12. The significance level is 0.05. Which of the following is the correct conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: There is convincing statistical evidence that the proportion of all students at the school who walk to school is exactly 0.30, as the null hypothesis states
choices.explanation: A test cannot show that the null hypothesis is true.

choices.label: B
choices.text: There is not convincing statistical evidence that the proportion of all students at the school who walk to school is different from 0.30
choices.explanation: Fail to reject H0: no convincing evidence for Ha.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The proportion of all students at the school who walk to school has been shown to be equal to 0.30 by the test
choices.explanation: Failing to reject H0 is not proof that H0 is true.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is convincing statistical evidence that the proportion of all students at the school who walk to school is different from 0.30
choices.explanation: The p-value is greater than α, so there is no convincing evidence of a difference.

explanation: p-value 0.12 > 0.05: fail to reject H0. We do not conclude that p = 0.30.

stem: A test of H₀: p = 0.50 versus Hₐ: p ≠ 0.50 gives z = -1.80. Which of the following is the p-value?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This doubles the two-sided p-value, which is already the sum of both tails.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The two-sided p-value is P(z ≤ -1.80) + P(z ≥ 1.80).

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is P(z ≥ -1.80), which is not a tail probability for this test.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This is the lower-tail p-value, for Hₐ: p < 0.50 only.

stem: In a hypothesis test, what is the meaning of the significance level α?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The probability that the null hypothesis is true
choices.explanation: The null hypothesis is either true or not. α is a probability about the decision rule.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The predetermined probability of rejecting the null hypothesis given that it is true
choices.explanation: The significance level is set before the data are collected.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The probability of getting the observed test statistic when the null hypothesis is true
choices.explanation: That is related to the p-value, which is computed from the data.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The probability of failing to reject the null hypothesis given that it is false
choices.explanation: That is the probability of a Type II error, not α.

explanation: α = P(reject H0 | H0 is true).

stem: A test has a p-value of 0.04. The researcher first planned to use α = 0.01, but then changed to α = 0.05 after seeing the p-value, so that the result would be significant. Which of the following is the best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The change is not needed, because with α = 0.01 the decision is to reject the null hypothesis
choices.explanation: 0.04 is greater than 0.01, so the decision is to fail to reject.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The significance level should be chosen in advance, and with α = 0.01 the decision is to fail to reject the null hypothesis
choices.explanation: Choosing α after seeing the result changes the meaning of the test.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The change is appropriate, because the researcher may select any significance level after seeing the p-value of the test
choices.explanation: The significance level is predetermined.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The change is appropriate, because a p-value of 0.04 is always significant
choices.explanation: Whether a result is significant depends on the α that was chosen in advance.

explanation: With the planned α = 0.01 and p-value 0.04, fail to reject H0.

stem: A company claims that 60% of its customers renew their membership. A random sample of 80 customers from a very large number of customers is selected, and 45 of them renew. A test of H₀: p = 0.60 versus Hₐ: p < 0.60 gives a test statistic z = -0.68 and a p-value of 0.247. At the 0.05 significance level, which of the following is the correct conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: There is convincing statistical evidence that the proportion of all of the company's customers who renew is less than 0.60
choices.explanation: The p-value, 0.247, is greater than 0.05, so the evidence is not convincing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: There is convincing statistical evidence that the proportion of all of the company's customers who renew is equal to 0.60
choices.explanation: A test cannot show that the null hypothesis is true.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There is not convincing statistical evidence for anything at all, because the sample proportion is not equal to 0.60 exactly
choices.explanation: The sample proportion is 0.5625. The question is whether that is enough evidence for Ha.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is not convincing statistical evidence that the proportion of all of the company's customers who renew is less than 0.60
choices.explanation: The p-value, 0.247, is greater than 0.05, so fail to reject H0.

stem: A test of H₀: p = 0.10 versus Hₐ: p > 0.10 is conducted, where p is the proportion of all patients who have a side effect from a medicine. Which of the following describes a Type I error?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Concluding that there is not convincing evidence that the proportion is greater than 0.10, when it is actually 0.10
choices.explanation: That is a correct conclusion, not an error.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Concluding that there is convincing evidence that the proportion of all patients with the side effect is greater than 0.10, when it is actually 0.10
choices.explanation: A Type I error is convincing evidence for the alternative when it is false.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Concluding that there is convincing evidence that the proportion is greater than 0.10, when it is actually greater than 0.10
choices.explanation: That is a correct conclusion, not an error.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Concluding that there is not convincing evidence that the proportion is greater than 0.10, when it is actually greater than 0.10
choices.explanation: That is a Type II error.

explanation: Type I: evidence for Ha that is not true.

stem: A test of H₀: p = 0.10 versus Hₐ: p > 0.10 is conducted, where p is the proportion of all patients who have a side effect from a medicine. Which of the following describes a Type II error?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Concluding that there is not convincing evidence that the proportion of all patients with the side effect is greater than 0.10, when it is actually greater than 0.10
choices.explanation: A Type II error is no convincing evidence for the alternative when the alternative is true.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Concluding that there is convincing evidence that the proportion of all patients who have the side effect is greater than 0.10, when it is actually 0.10
choices.explanation: That is a Type I error.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Concluding that there is convincing evidence that the proportion of all patients who have the side effect is 0.10, when it is actually greater than 0.10
choices.explanation: A test does not provide evidence for the null hypothesis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Concluding that there is not convincing evidence that the proportion is greater than 0.10, when it is actually 0.10
choices.explanation: That is a correct conclusion, not an error.

explanation: Type II: no convincing evidence for Ha although Ha is true.

stem: A hypothesis test is conducted at the significance level α = 0.01. Which of the following is the probability of a Type I error?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It cannot be determined without the sample size
choices.explanation: The probability of a Type I error is α, whatever the sample size.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The probability of a Type I error is the chosen α, 0.01.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is 1 - α, the probability of not rejecting a true null hypothesis.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The probability of a Type I error is the significance level.

explanation: P(Type I error) = α = 0.01.

stem: Which of the following is the best description of the power of a hypothesis test?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The probability that the test rejects the null hypothesis when the null hypothesis is true
choices.explanation: That is the probability of a Type I error, α.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The probability that the null hypothesis is false
choices.explanation: Power is a probability about the test, given the true value of the parameter.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The probability that the test fails to reject the null hypothesis when the null hypothesis is actually false
choices.explanation: That is the probability of a Type II error.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The probability that the test correctly rejects the null hypothesis when the null hypothesis is false
choices.explanation: Power is the probability of correctly rejecting a false null hypothesis.

explanation: Power = P(reject H0 | H0 is false) = 1 - P(Type II error).

stem: The power of a test against a specific alternative value is 0.85. What is the probability of a Type II error for that alternative value?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: P(Type II error) = 1 - power = 1 - 0.85.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The probability of a Type I error is α, which is not given, and it is not 1 - power.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the power, not the probability of a Type II error.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This would be 1 - α for α = 0.05, which does not apply here.

stem: A researcher wants to increase the power of a test of a population proportion, and nothing else about the study changes. Which of the following would increase the power?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increasing the sample size
choices.explanation: A larger sample reduces the standard error, which increases the power.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Choosing a null value that is closer to the true proportion
choices.explanation: When the true value is closer to the null value, the power is smaller.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decreasing the significance level α
choices.explanation: A smaller α makes it harder to reject the null hypothesis, which decreases the power.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decreasing the sample size of the study
choices.explanation: A smaller sample increases the standard error and decreases the power.

explanation: Power increases when the sample size increases.

stem: A test of a medicine's safety has the null hypothesis that the proportion of patients who have a dangerous side effect is at most 0.01. A Type II error would mean not detecting a medicine that is dangerous. Which of the following is the best recommendation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use a large sample size, since a Type II error has serious consequences and the sample size influences the probability of a Type II error
choices.explanation: The consequences of a Type II error influence the sample size.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use a very small significance level, since a Type II error has serious consequences and α is the probability of a Type II error in the test
choices.explanation: α is the probability of a Type I error, not of a Type II error.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use a small sample size, since a small sample reduces the probability of a Type II error
choices.explanation: A small sample increases the probability of a Type II error.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ignore the consequences of the errors, since the significance level should be chosen only as 0.05
choices.explanation: The consequences of each error should be considered before the study.

explanation: Consequences of a Type II error should influence the choice of the sample size (a larger n gives more power).

stem: A researcher increases the significance level of a test from 0.01 to 0.05, with everything else unchanged. Which of the following is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The probability of a Type I error increases and the probability of a Type II error decreases
choices.explanation: A larger α makes it easier to reject the null hypothesis, which raises the power.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The probability of a Type I error decreases and the probability of a Type II error increases
choices.explanation: The probability of a Type I error equals α, which increased.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The probabilities of both errors stay the same
choices.explanation: The probability of a Type I error is α, which changed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The probabilities of both errors increase
choices.explanation: A larger α decreases the probability of a Type II error.

explanation: Larger α: higher P(Type I), lower P(Type II) (higher power).

stem: Independent random samples of 200 adults from City A and 250 adults from City B are selected. In City A, the proportion of all adults who own a bicycle is 0.60, and in City B it is 0.50. What are the mean and the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of p̂₁ - p̂₂?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The mean is 0.10 and the standard deviation is 0.0663
choices.explanation: This adds the two standard deviations. The variances are added, and then the square root is taken.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The mean is 1.10 and the standard deviation is 0.0469
choices.explanation: The mean of the difference is the difference of the means, 0.60 - 0.50, not the sum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The mean is 0.10 and the standard deviation is 0.0469

choices.label: D
choices.text: The mean is 0.10 and the standard deviation is 0.0022
choices.explanation: This is the variance, before the square root is taken.

stem: Which of the following conditions must be met for the sampling distribution of p̂₁ - p̂₂ to be approximately normal when the data come from two independent random samples taken without replacement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The two sample sizes are equal, and the two population proportions are equal
choices.explanation: Neither is required. The sample sizes and the proportions can be different.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The two samples are dependent, and each sample has at least 5 successes and 5 failures
choices.explanation: The samples should be independent, and at least 10 successes and failures are needed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Each sample is at least 10% of its population, and the sample sizes are both greater than 30, so the counts do not matter
choices.explanation: Each sample should be at most 10% of its population, and the conditions use the counts of successes and failures.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Each sample is at most 10% of its population, and n₁p₁, n₁(1 - p₁), n₂p₂ and n₂(1 - p₂) are all at least 10
choices.explanation: These are the 10% condition for each sample and the expected counts of successes and failures in both samples.

explanation: Independent random samples, the 10% condition for each, and expected counts of at least 10 in all four cells.

stem: A researcher randomly assigns 120 volunteers to one of two treatments, 60 to each, and compares the proportions that improve. Which condition is needed for the sampling distribution of p̂₁ - p̂₂ to be used?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The volunteers must be a random sample from a population, and the 10% condition must be met
choices.explanation: In an experiment, the condition is on the random assignment, and the 10% condition is unnecessary.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The treatments must be randomly assigned to the volunteers; the 10% condition is not needed
choices.explanation: For an experiment, the data need to meet the randomization condition, and random assignment provides it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The volunteers must choose their treatment, so that each person is in the group that they prefer
choices.explanation: Choosing a treatment is not randomization. The treatments must be randomly assigned.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The two groups must be selected without replacement from populations that are at least 10 times larger
choices.explanation: The 10% condition is not needed for a randomized experiment.

explanation: For an experiment, randomization means random assignment of treatments; the 10% condition is unnecessary.

stem: The sampling distribution of p̂₁ - p̂₂ has a mean of 0.10 for independent random samples from City A and City B. Which of the following is the correct interpretation of the mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The proportion of adults in City A is 0.10 and the proportion of adults in City B is 0.10
choices.explanation: The mean describes the difference, 0.10, not each proportion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Over many pairs of random samples, the mean of the differences in the sample proportions, City A minus City B, is 0.10, which is p₁ - p₂
choices.explanation: The mean of the sampling distribution is the difference in the population proportions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The sample proportions for the two cities are each equal to 0.10 on average
choices.explanation: It is the difference between the sample proportions whose average is 0.10.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In every pair of random samples, the sample proportion for City A is exactly 0.10 greater than the sample proportion for City B in that pair
choices.explanation: The differences vary from one pair of samples to another.

explanation: Interpret the mean in context: the average difference over many pairs of samples.

stem: Independent random samples of 200 adults from City A (p₁ = 0.60) and 250 adults from City B (p₂ = 0.50) are selected. The sampling distribution of p̂₁ - p̂₂ is approximately normal with mean 0.10 and standard deviation 0.0469. What is the approximate probability that the sample proportion for City A is greater than the sample proportion for City B?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This would be the probability if the mean of the difference were 0. The mean is 0.10.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This doubles the standard deviation, which is not the standard deviation of the difference.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is P(z < -2.13), the probability that the sample proportion for City A is less than the sample proportion for City B.

stem: Both sample sizes are multiplied by 4, from 200 and 250 to 800 and 1,000, and the population proportions stay the same. What happens to the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of p̂₁ - p̂₂?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is divided by 2
choices.explanation: Each variance is divided by 4, so the variance of the difference is divided by 4 and the standard deviation is divided by 2.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It does not change
choices.explanation: The sample sizes are in the formula, so the standard deviation changes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is multiplied by 4
choices.explanation: Larger samples have less variability, so the standard deviation decreases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is divided by 4
choices.explanation: The standard deviation involves a square root, so it is divided by 2, not by 4.

explanation: σ is proportional to 1 / √n for both samples: it is divided by 2.

stem: Independent random samples of 40 adults from Town A and 60 adults from Town B are selected. The population proportions are p₁ = 0.15 and p₂ = 0.40. Is the sampling distribution of p̂₁ - p̂₂ approximately normal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No, because n₁p₁ = 40(0.15) = 6 is less than 10
choices.explanation: All four expected counts must be at least 10, and n₁p₁ = 6.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, because n₁ and n₂ are both greater than 30
choices.explanation: The conditions use the expected counts of successes and failures.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No, because the two sample sizes are not equal
choices.explanation: The sample sizes do not need to be equal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yes, because n₂p₂ = 60(0.40) = 24 is greater than 10
choices.explanation: All four expected counts must be at least 10, and the first is 6.

explanation: n1 p1 = 6 < 10, so the normal approximation is not appropriate.

stem: Independent random samples of students from two large schools are used to estimate the difference between the proportions of all students at the two schools who favor a later start time. Which procedure is appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A two-sample z-interval for a difference between population proportions
choices.explanation: The goal is to estimate p₁ - p₂ from two independent samples.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A two-sample z-test for a difference between population proportions
choices.explanation: A test is for evaluating a claim about the difference. The goal here is to estimate it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A chi-square test for independence
choices.explanation: A chi-square test is for categorical variables in a two-way table, and the goal here is an interval estimate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A one-sample z-interval for a population proportion
choices.explanation: There are two populations, so the parameter is a difference between two proportions.

explanation: Estimating p1 - p2 from two independent samples: a two-sample z-interval.

stem: Independent random samples from two large schools, School A and School B, are used to construct an interval for the difference in the proportions of all students at the schools who favor a later start time. Which of the following correctly states the parameter?

choices.label: A
choices.text: p₁ - p₂ = the difference between the number of students at the two schools who favor a later start time
choices.explanation: The parameter is a difference in proportions, not in counts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: p̂₁ - p̂₂ = the difference between the proportions of the students in the two samples who favor a later start time
choices.explanation: This is a statistic. The parameter is about the populations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: p₁ - p₂ = the difference between the proportion of all students at School A who favor a later start time and the proportion of all students at School B who favor a later start time
choices.explanation: The parameter refers to the difference, the response variable and both populations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: p = the proportion of all students at both schools who favor a later start time
choices.explanation: This is a single combined proportion, not a difference.

explanation: The parameter is the difference between the two population proportions, in context.

stem: Which of the following lists the conditions for a two-sample z-interval for a difference between two population proportions when the data come from two independent random samples taken without replacement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The two samples are paired; the population is approximately normal; and the sample sizes are each greater than 30
choices.explanation: The samples are independent, and the condition is on the counts of successes and failures.

choices.label: B
choices.text: One sample is random; the other is a convenience sample; and the counts of successes and failures are each at least 10
choices.explanation: Both samples must be random.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both samples are random and independent; each sample is at most 10% of its population; and the observed numbers of successes and failures in both samples are at least 10
choices.explanation: These are the randomization, 10% and normality conditions for two samples.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both samples are random; each sample is at least 10% of its population; and the numbers of observed successes and failures are at least 5 in each of the two samples
choices.explanation: The samples should be at most 10% of the populations, and the counts should be at least 10.

explanation: Randomization, the 10% condition for each sample, and at least 10 observed successes and failures in each.

stem: In a random sample of 200 students from School A, 120 favor a later start time. In an independent random sample of 220 students from School B, 90 favor a later start time. Which of the following is a 95% confidence interval for the difference between the proportions of all students at the two schools who favor a later start time, School A minus School B?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This adds the two standard errors instead of adding the variances and taking the square root.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is centered at the sample proportion for School A instead of at the difference in the proportions.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This uses z* = 1.645, which is for a 90% confidence level.

stem: In a random sample of 200 students from School A, 120 favor a later start time. In an independent random sample of 220 students from School B, 90 favor a later start time. What is the standard error of p̂₁ - p̂₂?

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This adds the two standard errors. The variances are added first.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This subtracts the standard errors. The variances of independent samples are added.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This is the variance of the difference, before the square root.

stem: A researcher randomly assigns 100 volunteers to a new exercise program and 100 volunteers to a control group. After 8 weeks, 45 of the volunteers in the program group and 30 of the volunteers in the control group have lowered their blood pressure. Which of the following is correct about the conditions for a two-sample z-interval for the difference in proportions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The normality condition is not met, because 30 is less than 45
choices.explanation: The counts do not need to be equal. They need to be at least 10.

choices.label: B
